title: Latency quirk brief and customer patch notes — 2027-03-02
body:
Purpose:
Quick synthesis of recent customer reports tied to increased tail latency for text-generation endpoints (hosted + dedicated). Goal: create a short list of patches we can trial in the next 2 sprints and capture customer-facing notes for CS handoffs. This is intentionally pragmatic — not a full RCA.

Summary (high-level):
- Root pattern: multiple customers report p99 spikes during multi-turn chat sessions and batch bursts. Issues appear more frequent when KV cache growth + long prefix prompts coincide with autoscale events.
- Affected product surfaces: Hosted API (tiered customers) and Dedicated pools with mixed-size models. Private deployments: a few on-prem customers reported similar symptoms but with environmental variance.

Representative customer snippets (redacted):
- "We see brief stalls where chat freezes for 3–7s, especially after long context replies — impacts UX heavily." — midmarket SaaS
- "P95 is OK but p99 kills the experience during demos." — enterprise search team

Immediate hypotheses (working):
1) KV cache eviction and rehydration on shard migration leads to temporary CPU/GPU stalls on the node and increases scheduling latency.
2) Autoscaling/placement decisions are occasionally picking nodes without warmed kernels (quantized variants), adding kernel load latency at request time.
3) Request batching heuristics degrade when mix of short control queries and long generation streams co-occur, producing head-of-line blocking.

Quick patches to trial (2-week cadence):
A) Soft-warm strategy for kernels: keep a minimal pool of warmed kernels for each model family on nodes that are candidates for assignment (experiment in dedicated small pool). Metric: reduce kernel-load component of per-request latency by 40–60%. Linked: GitHub PR/1987.
B) Prefix-length-aware batching cap: cap batch depth if the average prefix length > 1024 to avoid HL blocking. Metric: p95/p99 improvement for mixed workloads; trade-off on throughput to measure.
C) Staggered cache rehydration: when migrating shards, stream KV cache in background with prioritized tokens for active sessions. Metric: decrease session-stall reports. Requires coordination with serving-runtime team.
D) Canary fallback with lighter model variant (fewer kv pages) when node warming fails — customer-visible fallback path for critical SLAs.

Short impact estimates (back-of-envelope):
- A and B are low-risk, ~1 engineer-week each to prototype, ~2 engineer-weeks to test + roll to canary.
- C requires infra work (streaming protocol) and SRE involvement; medium effort (4–6 weeks).
- D is policy + routing changes; small-to-medium effort (3–4 weeks) but needs product sign-off.

Triage and prioritization (score rough):
- Customer severity (expected revenue impact): 7/10
- Frequency (how many incidents seen last 30d): 5/10
- Engineering effort: A(2) B(3) C(6) D(4) on relative scale (lower is easier)
- Quick-win priority: A then B, followed by D, then C.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Which models in the catalog are most sensitive to kernel warm-ups? Can runtime expose per-model kernel-load-time telemetry? (Ask: eng-observability)
- For dedicated customers, how often is autoscale causing cross-pool placements during business hours? Need hotpath traces.
- Are some customer SDK patterns (streaming vs non-streaming clients) exacerbating HL blocking? (CS to collect examples)

Action items (owners & next steps):
- Priya: Draft customer-facing FAQ explaining short-term mitigations and expected timelines; share with CS/AMs by 2027-03-11.
- Marco: Spin up PoC for kernel soft-warm PR (link above). Target alpha canary by 2027-03-22.
- Sofia: Run telemetry query for p50/p95/p99 split by model family and prefix-length bucket; report by 2027-03-16.
- Liam: Open a dedicated SRE checkpoint to evaluate eviction/re-hydration load; link to INF-4127 and add logs.
- CS team: Collect 3 reproducible customer sessions (anonymized) and attach to Jira as reproducer artifacts. Deadline: 2027-03-12.

Customer communications draft (short):
"Thanks for flagging this. We’ve identified a set of mitigations we’re trialing to reduce tail stalls — a short warm-up patch and a batching configuration change are highest priority. We’ll share canary timelines and, where appropriate, enable temporary fallbacks while we validate fixes."

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep this doc short; move long RCA content into INF-4127.
- Possible related: see product/hosted-api/latency-sla-profiles (confluence).
- Slack threads: #cust-ops (p99-incident-2027-02-28), #runtime-kernel.

Appendix: telemetry queries and quick charts we should run (examples):
- p99 by hour + autoscale event tags (last 30d).
- p99 vs prefix-length buckets (0–512, 513–1024, 1025–2048, 2049+).
- Kernel-load time distribution per model and per hardware type.

If anyone reading wants to add customer quotes or link more tickets, append below and ping me.

-- Priya
